subject: MSA: output assignment vs feedback license — coordination and next steps
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@clearwave.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Clearsys Legal <legal@clearwave.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines on MSA + order form (output assignment / feedback license)

Hi Rishi —

Attached are the redlines from our legal team on the MSA and the order form. Two principal points surfaced that we need your input on:

1) Output assignment: the clause currently attempts to assign title to outputs to the customer for productization. Our counsel is pushing for explicit carveouts for Redwood telemetry and model improvement usage.

2) Feedback license: they want a perpetual, royalty-free license to use customer-provided feedback and data to retrain models. We flagged that as too broad and asked for a scoped, non-exclusive license limited to anonymized aggregate improvements.

Can you confirm who on your side should be looped in for legal/ops tradeoffs (e.g., whether we can offer a narrower feedback license or provide a telemetry-only exemption)? We also prefer a short call next week with redlines on screen.

Attachments: Clearwave_MSA_redlines_20260417.pdf, OrderForm_CW_v3_redline.docx

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Procurement, Clearwave Systems
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@clearwave.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redlines on MSA + order form (output assignment / feedback license)

Ben / Laura —

Looping you both in; customer sent redlines that expand customer title to outputs and a broad feedback license. Quick notes from my read:

- Output assignment: Clearwave wants assignment "for any output produced by the Service" which is dangerously broad. We typically offer a customer-specific license for their outputs and an explicit carveout that Redwood may use aggregated telemetry and model improvements (with an anonymity/aggregation requirement).

- Feedback license: their draft is perpetual and worldwide. We should propose: (a) scoped license limited to non-personal, de-identified feedback; (b) allow opt-out for training on a per-environment basis; (c) limited SAML/event telemetry still allowed for service ops and quality.

Recommended next steps:
- Laura: can legal run a one-page alternative clause for the output assignment that converts assignment -> exclusive license for cleared outputs + carveout for model improvement?
- Ben: pricing/sales — if customer insists on assignment we should propose a premium (reserved capacity / enterprise price) or an escrow/process we can accept.
- I'll coordinate a 30-min sync with Clearwave next Wed (status: pending time confirmation).

Ben — want me to propose language or do you want legal to draft?

Rishi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@clearwave.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redlines on MSA + order form (output assignment / feedback license)

Quick answers —

Rishi, appreciate the call-to-action. I agree with the approach. A few practical points from pricing/ops:

- If Clearwave keeps assignment, they will expect unencumbered downstream use (including sublicensing to their customers). That materially increases commercial risk; we should model the delta.
- Proposal: offer a narrow assignment only for outputs generated by their private/dedicated deployment when they provide an explicit training opt-out. Public/hosted outputs cannot be assigned.
- If they require a perpetual feedback license, propose time-boxed term (e.g., 3 years) for model retraining plus the ability to opt-out per dataset.

I can draft a short bullets doc for the call that summarizes these concessions + pricing premiums. Laura — can you prepare a redline alternative for the 'feedback license' paragraph and one for 'output assignment' before Wednesday? If legal is tight, I can escalate to SVP Sales to sign off on discounts vs term.

Ben
Director, Sales Operations
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@clearwave.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redlines on MSA + order form (output assignment / feedback license)

Maya / team —

Thanks for the redlines and call invite. Per our internal review (summary below) and attached suggestions, here are concrete alternatives we can discuss on the sync: 

1) Output assignment: we cannot accept a blanket assignment for hosted model outputs. Alternative A (preferred): customer receives an exclusive, transferable license to outputs produced from customer input when using Redwood Dedicated or Private (customer-controlled environment). For Hosted API usage, Redwood retains rights to aggregate outputs and any model improvements.

2) Feedback license: alternative language attached narrows scope to "de-identified, aggregated feedback" and is limited to a 36-month term for retraining purposes. We include an opt-out mechanism (per-environment) and a telemetry-only carveout for operational debugging.

3) Order form: if Clearwave requires assignment for hosted outputs, we propose a commercial concession — a one-time fee + elevated support SLA (details in attachment).

Attachments: Proposed_Output_Clause_v1.docx, Feedback_License_Alt_v1.docx

Please confirm availability for a 30-min call on Wed 28 Apr 2026 between 08:30–11:00 PT. If you want to proceed without a call we can circulate the redlines and a short memo for decision.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Proposed_Output_Clause_v1.docx (redline), Feedback_License_Alt_v1.docx (redline)"
